verdictStatement: Codex's blocker is closed on four of its five evidence bullets, and closed well. signedBinding gives the install-root input a name, scope, value type, a closed serialization, an anchor that rides exact-byte delivery and DR-G07, an equality rule, and a refusal while the upstream identity is absent — with 'This artifact does not invent that identity', which is the right restraint. canonicalization states symlink resolution once and declares the canonical path the only input to both OS branches, and targetPath.not expressly rules out ordinary host path resolution, a second live re-read, and later object paths, which closes my own CLAUDE-V9-S1. The Linux comparison now decodes kernel octal escapes and matches on component-ancestor prefixes with 'String prefix on undecoded bytes is not the comparison', answering the /opt/app versus /opt/application case exactly. sameVolume decides the ambiguity Codex found in step 3 in the strong direction — exact volume identity by f_fsid on macOS and by decoded mount-point plus device on Linux, retained alongside the type token, with both compared and a refusal if either comparison cannot be made — and resolutionPredicate step 3 is rewritten to execute it. companionObservation becomes mandatory whenever a signed sonameAbi companion is present, with three closed forms that require the observed pair on present and mismatch. What holds acceptance is smaller than any of that: the one signed binding point is still located on 'the profile/carrier' rather than on one of them, the verifier's process identity is the single term in the block left undefined against the reuse case Codex named, and the ledger's disposition entry still certifies the v8 cycle at v10.

measurement.codexObjectedToThisPhrase: PTCB-V9-B1's first evidence bullet reads in part "'profile/carrier' therefore asserts a binding without selecting or provisioning its one binding point", and its requiredRepair opens 'Define exactly one signed preselection binding point'. v10 supplies every attribute that repair listed — name, scope, closed value type and serialization, anchor, equality — but keeps the disjunction about where the binding lives.

The field does not exist until that one DR-101 successor authors it.' The token verifiedInstallRoot occurs five times, all inside filesystemMeasurementTarget or the repair log, and nowhere in either structure.
measurement.theBranchesDiffer: This is not a harmless disjunction. If the binding is on the profile, a key that is frozen and reused across runs acquires a deployment-specific install-root path, which is at odds with the slice-profile model of osFamily, architecture, version selector and filesystem member. If it is on the carrier, this row is adding a field to the one signed inventory carrier whose sole author is the DR-101 successor — the singular-authorship discipline tcbCarrier.inventoryFieldAuthor has guarded since v3, and which the same object elsewhere protects with 'Not a slash-joined owner of the inventory field.'
measurement.lineagePrecedent: The artifact's own standard rejects slash-joined designations: signatureCeremonyOwner carries that sentence because Codex objected at PTCB-V3-S1 to the carrier being 'owned by DR-101/DR-103'. The same objection applies to a binding point located on 'the profile/carrier'.

shouldFix.consequence: The measurement algorithm is fully determined once the value exists, so this does not make the target non-reproducible and is not a blocker. What is undetermined is which signed artifact holds and signs the value, and one of the two readings collides with the singular-carrier-authorship rule.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Pick one. Either state that verifiedInstallRoot is a field of the signed carrier and say how it coexists with inventoryFieldAuthor's single-author rule, or state that it is a signed profile-level input distinct from the four selector members and say plainly that it is not part of the platformProfileKey. Then delete the slash.

shouldFix.title: The verifier's process identity is recorded but never defined, so the /proc/<verifierPid> read is unprotected against reuse

measurement.againstTheFrozenRequirement: PTCB-V9-B1's fifth evidence bullet reads that the contract 'defines neither the profile field nor the process-identity equality that binds a /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo read against PID reuse or process replacement', and its requiredRepair says 'For Linux, bind the stable process/mount-namespace identity … and detect retargeting.'
measurement.whatLanded: The profile-field half is repaired and repaired correctly: observerProcess now says the identities are 'recorded on the qualification run, not on the frozen profile', and retainedEventSchema gains observerProcessIdentity and mountNamespaceIdentity as fields fifteen and sixteen, the latter carrying its own comparison rule. Namespace binding is enforced per event and retargeting is detected on the (decoded mount-point, device) pair.
measurement.whatDidNot: No definition or equality rule is given for process identity. The term appears only as the bare phrase 'Its process identity' and as the schema field name. A PID alone is not a stable identity; the standard ways to make it one — pid plus start time, a pidfd, or checking the namespace inode before the read — are not named. Every other term in this block is now defined to the code point: NFC, POSIX separators, no empty or dot components, kernel octal escape decoding, component-ancestor prefixes, f_fsid, (decoded mount-point, device) pairs.
measurement.whyTheNamespaceCheckDoesNotCoverIt: mountNamespaceIdentity protects later events by comparison against the recorded baseline. It cannot protect the preselection read itself: if <verifierPid> is reused between the moment the verifier process is named and the moment an independent observer opens /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo, the observer reads a different process, records that namespace as the baseline, and every later comparison then agrees with the wrong baseline.

shouldFix.consequence: A qualification run can be anchored to the wrong mount namespace while every stated check passes. Narrow and racy rather than routine, but it is the one element of the frozen requiredRepair that did not land, in a block where everything else is exact.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Define process identity as a closed pair — for example pid plus process start time, or a pidfd held open across the read — and state the equality. Require the observer to verify that identity immediately before and after reading /proc/<verifierPid>/mountinfo, and refuse on mismatch.

repairVerification.detail: This is my own S-1 and it is closed the way I asked. canonicalization.rule states the resolution once — 'Canonicalize verifiedInstallRoot once, here, before any measurement. Resolve every symbolic-link component. The canonical path is the only path input to macOS statfs and to the Linux mount-point prefix match' — with a refusal for any path that cannot be canonicalized to exactly one path. The conflicting derivation clause is gone: targetPath now has only is and not, and not expressly excludes 'ordinary host path resolution, a second live re-read of the install root, or a later object path'. macos.interface and linux.recordSelection both consume the canonical path explicitly, so the two branches no longer diverge on symlink handling.

repairVerification.claim: Linux decoded component-ancestor comparison and retargeting — PTCB-V9-B1 bullet 3
repairVerification.detail: mountPointDecoding requires decoding kernel octal escapes for space, tab, newline and backslash before any comparison. recordSelection becomes 'over decoded mount points, the record whose mount-point is the longest component-ancestor prefix of the canonical targetPath; if several records share that mount point, the last such record in file order. String prefix on undecoded bytes is not the comparison', which is precisely Codex's /opt/app versus /opt/application counterexample and its raw-spelling point. retargeting adds refusal if the selected record's (decoded mount-point, device) pair changes between preselection and a later resolution.

The rule sentence is also tightened from 'satisfy this same designated targetPath' to occupying 'the same target volume as the unique volume that contains targetPath'.

coordinatorNote: This is the best generation in the lineage and the second consecutive one with no blockers. Codex's five-bullet blocker is closed on four bullets, and closed by construction rather than by wording: the install-root input now has a name, a closed serialization, an anchor that rides DR-G07 with an explicit refusal while that upstream identity is absent, a single canonicalization consumed by both OS branches, decoded component-ancestor mount matching that answers the /opt/app versus /opt/application case exactly, retargeting detection on the (mount-point, device) pair, and a decided exact-volume comparison that step 3 was rewritten to execute. Codex's SHOULD-FIX on the companion is closed on both of its holes. My own two SHOULD-FIX items are closed, the second one in the way I asked — the identities moved off the frozen profile and onto the qualification run and the retained event schema. What is left is genuinely small but real. The one signed binding point is still located on 'the profile/carrier', which is the slash-joined form this lineage has rejected before and which neither the four-member profile key nor the carrier's binding point currently provisions; the two branches have different and material consequences, one of them touching the singular-carrier-authorship rule. Process identity is the single term in an otherwise code-point-exact block that is left undefined, and it is precisely the element Codex named against PID reuse; the namespace comparison protects later events but cannot protect the preselection read that establishes the baseline. And the ledger's disposition entry still certifies the v8 cycle in a generation that folds v9, in a field that was rostered and edited this round. None of the three requires new design work. DR-126 stays OPEN, no row of any number is marked SATISFIED, all four D-096 occurrences are prohibitions, no per-OS table is populated, and nothing here qualifies G22 or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/. The subject, prompt, file 08 and COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md were not edited and nothing was committed.
